Main.sentence: NATO victory
___E:NATO U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NATO)___ -led coalition

Operation Unified Protector was a ___E:NATO U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NATO)___ operation in 2011 enforcing ___E:United Nations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations)___ ___E:Security Council U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Security_Council)___ ___E:resolutions U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Security_Council_resolution)___ ___E:1970 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Security_Council_Resolution_1970)___ and ___E:1973 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Security_Council_Resolution_1973)___ concerning the ___E:Libyan Civil War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Libyan_Civil_War_(2011))___ and adopted on 26 February and 17 March 2011, respectively.

These resolutions imposed sanctions on key members of the ___E:Gaddafi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muammar_Gaddafi)___ government and authorized NATO to implement an ___E:arms embargo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arms_embargo)___ , a ___E:no-fly zone U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No-fly_zone)___ and to use all [citation needed] means necessary, short of foreign ___E:occupation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_occupation)___ , to protect Libyan civilians and civilian populated areas.  [non-primary source needed]

The operation started on 23 March 2011 and gradually expanded during the following weeks, by integrating more and more elements of the multinational ___E:military intervention U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_military_intervention_in_Libya)___ , which had started on 19 March in response to the same UN resolutions.
As of 31 March 2011 it encompassed all international operations in ___E:Libya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Libya)___ .
NATO support was vital to the rebel victory over the forces loyal to Gaddafi.

The operation officially ended on 31 October 2011, after the rebel leaders, formalized in the ___E:National Transitional Council U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Transitional_Council)___ , had declared Libya liberated on 23 October.

The operation began with a naval arms embargo, while command of the ___E:no-fly zone U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No-fly_zone)___ and the air strikes against ___E:Libyan Armed Forces U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armed_forces_of_the_Libyan_Arab_Jamahiriya)___ remained under command of the international coalition, led by ___E:France U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France)___ , the ___E:United Kingdom U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom)___ and the ___E:United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States)___ , due to lack of consensus between NATO members.  [non-primary source needed] On 24 March NATO decided to take control of the ___E:no-fly zone U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No-fly_zone)___ enforcement, by integrating the air assets of the international coalition under NATO command, although the command of air strikes on ground targets remained under national authority.  [non-primary source needed]  A few days later, on 27 March NATO decided to implement all military aspects of the UN resolution and formal transfer of command occurred at 06:00 ___E:GMT U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greenwich_Mean_Time)___ on 31 March 2011, formally ending the national operations such as the U.S.-coordinated ___E:Operation Odyssey Dawn U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Odyssey_Dawn)___ .  [non-primary source needed]

The arms embargo was initially carried out using mainly ships from NATO's ___E:Standing Maritime Group 1 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standing_NRF_Maritime_Group_1)___ and ___E:Standing Mine Countermeasures Group 1 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standing_NRF_Mine_Countermeasures_Group_1)___ already patrolling the ___E:Mediterranean Sea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mediterranean_Sea)___ at the time of the resolution, enforced with additional ships, submarines and maritime surveillance aircraft from NATO members.

They were to "monitor, report and, if needed, ___E:interdict U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interdiction)___ vessels suspected of carrying ___E:illegal arms U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arms_trafficking)___ or ___E:mercenaries U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercenary)___ ".
The no-fly zone was enforced by aircraft transferred to Unified Protector from the international coalition, with additional aircraft from NATO and other allied nations.
The air strikes, although under central NATO command, were only conducted by aircraft of the nations agreeing to enforce this part of the UN resolution.

With Operation Unified Protector, NATO is involved in an internal Libyan conflict, between those seeking to depose the country's long-time national leader ___E:Muammar Gaddafi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muammar_Gaddafi)___ and pro-Gaddafi forces.

The conflict began as a series of non-peaceful disorders, part of the broader ___E:Arab Spring U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab_Spring)___ movement, which Gaddafi's security services attempted to repress, but which soon developed into a widespread uprising.

The situation further escalated into armed conflict, with rebels establishing a provisional government named the ___E:National Transitional Council U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Transitional_Council)___ based in eastern city of ___E:Benghazi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benghazi)___ and controlling the eastern part of the country and the western city of ___E:Misrata U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misrata)___ .

The ___E:International Criminal Court U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Criminal_Court)___ warned Gaddafi that he and members of his government may have committed crimes against humanity.

The ___E:United Nations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations)___ ___E:Security Council U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Security_Council)___ passed an initial ___E:resolution U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Security_Council_resolution)___ ___E:1970 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Security_Council_Resolution_1970)___ , freezing the assets of ___E:Gaddafi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaddafi)___ and ten members of his inner circle, and restricting their travel.
The resolution also referred the actions of the government to the ___E:International Criminal Court U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Criminal_Court)___ for investigation.

In early March, Gaddafi's forces rallied, pushed eastwards and re-took several coastal cities and finally began attacking the rebel stronghold of ___E:Benghazi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benghazi)___ on 19 March 2011. Two days earlier a second U.N. resolution, ___E:UNSC Resolution 1973 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Security_Council_Resolution_1973)___ , was passed which authorized member states to establish and enforce an arms embargo, a no-fly zone over Libya and to use all means necessary, short of foreign ___E:occupation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_occupation)___ , to protect Libyan civilians.  [non-primary source needed] In response to the resolution, the Gaddafi government announced a ceasefire, but failed to uphold it and continued to advance on the rebels and the ___E:Second Battle of Benghazi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Battle_of_Benghazi)___ began.

In response to the U.N. resolution, voted on 17 March 2011, an international coalition was established and naval and air forces were quickly deployed in and around the ___E:Mediterranean Sea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mediterranean_Sea)___ .

Two days later, on 19 March, France intervened in the imminent ___E:Second Battle of Benghazi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Battle_of_Benghazi)___ with air strikes on Gaddafi armor and troops and eventually forced them back. On the same day 110 ___E:Tomahawk cruise missiles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomahawk_(missile_family))___ were launched from UK and US ships, further air strikes against ground targets were executed and a naval blockade was established.
The initial coalition consisted of Belgium, Canada, Denmark, France, Italy, Norway, Qatar, Spain, the United Kingdom and the United States.

The official names for the interventions by the coalition members are ___E:Opération Harmattan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Op%C3%A9ration_Harmattan)___ by France; ___E:Operation Ellamy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Ellamy)___ by the United Kingdom; ___E:Operation Mobile U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Mobile)___ for the Canadian participation and ___E:Operation Odyssey Dawn U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Odyssey_Dawn)___ for the United States.

The U.S. initially coordinated the effort and took strategic and tactical command at ___E:UCC U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unified_Combatant_Command)___ ___E:USAFRICOM U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Africa_Command)___ , led by ___E:Carter Ham U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carter_Ham)___ , and the Joint Task Force Odyssey Dawn, led by ___E:Samuel J. Locklear U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuel_J._Locklear)___ aboard the ___E:command ship U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Command_ship)___ ___E:USS Mount Whitney (LCC-20) U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Mount_Whitney)___ , respectively.

From there on command was split between the air and naval components of the operation at which level the different participating countries commanded their assets in accordance with their ___E:rules of engagement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rules_of_engagement)___ and through ___E:liaison officers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liaison_officer)___ .

After the initial intervention, the U.S. wanted to scale down their involvement significantly to a supporting role. Due to lack of consensus within ___E:NATO U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NATO)___ , the only other body capable of commanding a multinational operation of this size, however, this was not possible immediately.
As consensus grew during the next days, NATO took more and more parts of the operation under its command until taking command of all military operations on 31 March.

Political direction is provided by the ___E:North Atlantic Council U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Atlantic_Council)___ to the ___E:Supreme Headquarters Allied Powers Europe U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Headquarters_Allied_Powers_Europe)___ .

The chain of command is from ___E:Supreme Allied Commander Europe U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Allied_Commander_Europe)___ , Admiral ___E:James G. Stavridis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_G._Stavridis)___ (US Navy), to the Deputy Commander of ___E:Allied Joint Force Command Naples U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allied_Joint_Force_Command_Naples)___ , Lt. General ___E:Charles Bouchard U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Bouchard)___ ( ___E:Royal Canadian Air Force U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Canadian_Air_Force)___ ) acting as operational commander.

From the operational level, command is further delegated to the Commander of Allied Maritime Command Naples, Vice Admiral ___E:Rinaldo Veri U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rinaldo_Veri)___ (Italian Navy) for the naval operations and Commander of Allied Air Command Izmir, Lieutenant General ___E:Ralph J. Jodice II U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ralph_J._Jodice_II)___ (US Air Force) for air operations.
